competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move. Supported STIR contracts use exchange DV01 and currency conversion; historical rows without that stamp keep the legacy duration-one vintage and are not silently restated. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

research_supplement.summary: Overnight sentiment stayed defensive as October’s hotter-than-expected CPI and hawkish Fed rhetoric kept December rate-hike pricing firm, pressuring Treasuries and supporting the dollar narrative in the headline flow. Frozen marks still show elevated crude—WTI near $86.53 and Brent near $92.76—with gold around $4,000.50, while U.S. benchmarks sit at roughly 7,521 on the S&P 500, 25,466 on the Nasdaq, and 52,486 on the Dow amid a sub-20 VIX. Chicago Fed President Goolsbee called the inflation report “borderline disturbing,” reinforcing fears of a larger hike, while Williams argued the Fed should gather more information on price risks. Energy headlines highlighted jet-fuel pain and Gulf routing shifts as oil import patterns adjust. Watch for the next U.S. inflation and housing prints, further Fedspeak, and whether high crude prices broaden into corporate margins; official BoC framework language and dated Fed operational remarks offer little near-term policy offset.

postmortems.thesis_assessment: The NZDUSD long was a bounce off 0.56 that never extended. It was scratched at the entry, and by this cutoff March 2027 SOFR is 4.53, through 4.435, with NZDUSD at 0.5584.
postmortems.what_failed: The bounce failed to extend, but the pre-committed exit contained it at the entry price. The miss was using NZD spot to express a view whose real trigger was the US front end.
postmortems.no_new_lesson: This was bounded variance around a rule that already existed. The invalidation was a full retrace of the bounce or March 2027 SOFR through 4.435 in a dollar squeeze, and the scratch followed that rule before the cross could become a loss. The prior process remains sound: do not reopen NZDUSD while that dollar-squeeze condition is live, and keep the pro-growth expression in the rates book.

causal.original_belief: A long NZDUSD from 0.56 would extend if global risk appetite stayed intact and the bounce held.
causal.observed_reality: The long was exited at 0.56. NZDUSD is now 0.5584, March 2027 SOFR is 4.53, and the dollar is breaking up against the euro, the Australian dollar, and the Canadian dollar while equities and VIX have not signaled a growth break.
causal.assumptions_right: Defining the invalidation as a full bounce retrace or SOFR March 2027 through 4.435 gave a clear exit. Equity risk appetite was not the thing that broke: the S&P is still 7520.93 and VIX is 19.46.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Underweighted how fast a hot US inflation path would dominate a small NZD bounce through the dollar, and treated NZD spot as a substitute for the rates view once SOFR was the actual invalidation gauge.
causal.causal_divergence: The bounce was a fade of a dollar squeeze. The squeeze resumed because the US front end repriced higher, so the long never left the entry and the later spot is softer.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same growth view and the same SOFR invalidation level, the position to keep was the US front-end short, not a new NZDUSD long.
causal.future_implication: Leave NZDUSD alone while March 2027 SOFR holds above 4.435. The held SOFR, AONIA, and CORRA payers are the expression of resilient nominal growth.

postmortems.what_failed: The March 2027 SOFR receive was a fade of a hike reprice that never reversed. Implied yield rose from 4.33 at entry on 2 November to 4.53 at the 11 November exit. postmortems.thesis_assessment: The receive assumed the easing path was still the persistent trend and that 4.33 was a level to own. The persistent move was higher implied yields. The invalidation was the right kill-switch. The error was the original side, not the decision to get out once the curve had reversed higher together.
postmortems.lesson: Do not receive SOFR in front of a live hike reprice. A receive is only a trend trade after the front end has actually reversed. When March implied is printing higher and the two-year and ten-year are reversing higher together, the trend is higher yields and the receive is a premature fade.
postmortems.future_rule: Do not open or hold a SOFR receive once the US two-year reclaims 4.67, or once that contract's implied is rising while the curve reverses higher together. Stand with the higher-yield trend until one of those conditions breaks.

causal.original_belief: March 2027 SOFR implied would hold or fall from 4.33, so a receive was with the prevailing path, and a two-year reclaim of 4.67 was a distant invalidation rather than the base case.

causal.assumptions_right: The invalidation was observable and correctly joint: March implied higher plus the curve reversing higher was the right condition to abandon the receive. Exiting on that print stopped the fade against a move that was already broad.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The persistence of the selloff in yields was underweighted, and so was the inflation reaction function. Entry at 4.33 treated a still-rising implied as a receive level.
causal.causal_divergence: The book was receiving while the macro impulse and the curve were moving toward a higher policy path. The gap between belief and outcome is the direction of the implied yield, from 4.33 to 4.53, with cash yields confirming rather than diverging.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same information, a rule that refuses a new receive while the front end is still reversing higher would have left this book flat or paying. It would not have worn the receive from 4.33 to 4.53.
causal.future_implication: The next expression has to stand with the higher-yield and stronger-dollar trend. Do not re-receive SOFR. Do not pay the ten-year at 4.98 without a confirmed new yield high.

postmortems.what_worked: The short was opened at 1.25 on 3 November with invalidation if the cross held through 1.255, if Australian implied tightening repriced the Aussie higher versus the kiwi, or if a one-way commodity shock hit. None of those conditions printed during the hold. The cross fell and the short was closed at 1.23 on 11 November.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The belief that 1.25 was an unstable extreme was confirmed by the decline to 1.23. The close matched the preservation rule of taking the break rather than converting a finished short into a lower-entry add-on. Firm Brent at 92.76 is the commodity condition that argued against staying short even though the cross ticked a little lower after the exit.
postmortems.lesson: A cross short that has already fallen through the entry extreme is a completed expression. Re-opening it just below the exit, into a failed nearby floor while commodities are bid and other shorts are covering, treats a finished trade as a new one.
postmortems.future_rule: Do not re-open a closed cross short in the same swing unless price resets to a fresh extreme and the original invalidation is clearly not in force. A failed floor, peer covering, or a firm commodity tape is a reason to stay flat until a new extreme exists.

causal.original_belief: AUDNZD at 1.25 was extended and would fall unless it held through 1.255, Australian implied tightening repriced the Aussie up versus the kiwi, or a one-way commodity shock arrived.
causal.observed_reality: From 3 November to 11 November the cross fell from 1.25 to 1.23 and the short was closed after that fall. It now sits at 1.2285 on a failed 20-day floor, with Brent at 92.76 and other desks closing small shorts.
causal.assumptions_right: The cross had room to fall from 1.25 without a fresh relative-rate shock interrupting the window, and a defined extreme plus a hard invalidation was the right expression.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: How little residual would remain once 1.23 traded was underweighted, as was the chance that a firm commodity tape would make any add-on a different trade from the original extreme.
causal.causal_divergence: Price and the short thesis agreed: the cross fell and the invalidations did not hit. The only gap versus a larger target is the small slip from the 1.23 exit to 1.2285, which is not a new signal.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: On the 3 November information, the short at 1.25 with invalidation through 1.255 was still the position to hold. Re-shorting after the close, once the cross had already fallen and oil was firm, would not have been the same trade.
causal.future_implication: Keep the extreme-and-invalidate framework and the habit of closing once the cross has fallen. Do not recycle this short at 1.2285.
